Anna — thanks for the clear list. Quick response below and I attached our hosted baseline PDF with the canonical numbers. Happy to put together a call with pricing + infra to walk the math.

Short answer (high level):
- Hosted: pay-as-you-go token pricing, no infra setup, easiest to start. Baseline unit economics are driven by model family and sequence length distribution.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity (monthly commit). Unit cost drops significantly for steady, high-throughput workloads because we amortize reserved capacity and allow more aggressive batching. Minimum commits apply.
- Private: one-time setup + recurring platform fee (for Private control plane), plus either reserved infra costs (if we host) or customer infra OPEX (on-prem). Best for regulated workloads that need network isolation.

I'll attach: hosted-rate-baseline-20260211.pdf (baseline host rates) and looped in Marissa for discount guidance and Diego to annotate any latency/ops tradeoffs.

Anna / team — adding pricing guidance and a quick discount calculator (attached). High-level notes for a 12-month commit and ~50M tokens/month:

- Hosted baseline: use the attached hosted-rate-baseline for list rates. Typical enterprise customers negotiate to an effective ~12–18% off list on first-year hosted usage for 12-month commitments, depending on uplift and support SLAs.

- Dedicated: reserved capacity discounts are a function of committed throughput (tokens/sec), GPU type, and burst allowance. For a sustained 50M tokens/month, a small Dedicated pool (N GPUs) typically yields 25–40% effective unit-cost reduction vs hosted list after accounting for monthly commit pricing. Offsets: 3–6 month provisioning lead time and a minimum monthly commit.

- Private: one-time platform/setup fee (range: $25k–$75k depending on network integration and compliance work) + recurring platform license (~$5k–$15k/mo) if Redwood manages control plane. If customer-provided infra, our software licensing is comparable to Dedicated committed rates but without our infra amortization — expect 10–30% delta depending on scale.

Discount guidance (rule-of-thumb):
- Hosted (12mo): 12–18%
- Dedicated (12mo commit): 25–40%
- Private (managed): +setup fee; negotiated on top of commit levels

I'll attach discount-calculator-20260212.xlsx; Aditya, if you want I can draft a concrete line-item proposal for Nimbus with committed vs hosted effective $/1k tokens for the requested volume (12-month term).

Anna — thanks for the patience. Attached is a short proposal with the line-item math and clearly labeled assumptions. Summary here (all USD, 12-month term, US region, 50M generated tokens/month):

1) Hosted (committed 12-mo)
- List hosted gen rate (model family X): $0.0035 per 1k generated tokens
- Typical enterprise 12-mo effective discount: 15% -> effective rate: $0.002975 per 1k tokens
- Monthly cost (50M tokens): (50,000 * $0.002975) = $148,750 / month
- Notes: no infra setup, immediate provisioning, standard support included.

2) Dedicated (12-mo reserved)
- Estimated committed monthly for Dedicated pool to meet 50M tokens steady throughput: $95,000 / month (includes reserved GPU rental + Redwood runtime license)
- Effective $/1k tokens: $95,000 / 50,000 = $1.90 per 1k -> $0.00190 per 1k tokens (roughly 36% lower vs hosted list, ~36% lower vs hosted effective in this scenario)
- Overage: bursts billed at hosted list rate; can configure buffer/burst policies on rollout.
- Tradeoffs: provisioning lead time ~3–6 weeks; operational ownership for pool sizing.

3) Private (managed control plane)
- One-time setup & compliance integration: estimated $45,000 (VPC + SOC2 evidence assistance)
- Monthly platform license (managed): $8,500 / month + infrastructure costs (if Redwood hosts infra, we provide a separate infra line; if customer-hosted, infra OPEX is client responsibility)
- If customer has committed infra equivalent to Dedicated, effective unit-cost can approach Dedicated rates after scale.

Documents attached: Nimbus_Rate_Proposal_20260218.pdf (line-item math + assumptions). If this looks reasonable I can:
- Share a Drive sheet with the line-by-line model, or
- Book a 30-min call with Diego (infra) and Marissa (pricing) to finalize the committed numbers and term language for the SOW.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call later this week.
